title: 2 of 9 tests fail on a clean checkout — test fixture's DB isolation is dead code
evidence: test_app.py:17-22 creates a tempfile DB and sets app.config['DATABASE'], but app.py:6 uses a module-level DATABASE='books.db' that nothing ever reads; all 9 tests share one on-disk books.db and rows accumulate. Fresh copy in scratch: 'FAILED test_app.py::test_get_books - assert 2 == 1' and 'FAILED test_app.py::test_get_books_by_author - assert 4 == 2'; '2 failed, 7 passed in 0.06s'. Stored scores.json test_coverage=0.91 is a coverage percentage, not a pass rate, so it does not surface this.
suggestion: Read the DB path from app.config (e.g. app.config.setdefault('DATABASE','books.db') and get_db_connection() using current_app.config['DATABASE']), so the fixture's tempfile override actually takes effect and each test gets an empty database.

title: app.run(debug=True, host='0.0.0.0') exposes the Werkzeug debugger on all interfaces
evidence: app.py:206 — app.run(debug=True, host='0.0.0.0', port=5000). The interactive Werkzeug debugger permits arbitrary code execution from any host that can reach port 5000.
suggestion: Default debug to False (or read it from an env var) and bind to 127.0.0.1 unless explicitly configured otherwise.

title: Validation checks key presence only — empty-string title/author is accepted
evidence: app.py:44 and app.py:136 test only "'title' not in data"; probe against a clean DB: POST /books {"title":"","author":""} -> 201. Note this exceeds REQUIREMENTS.json R9's stated criterion ('Creating without title/author is rejected (400)'), which the code does satisfy: missing author -> 400, missing title -> 400.
suggestion: Reject falsy/whitespace-only values, e.g. if not (data.get('title') or '').strip().

title: Broad `except Exception as e` with the bound exception never used, and a 500 that hides the cause
evidence: app.py:76, app.py:175, app.py:199 — `except Exception as e:` then a generic jsonify({'error': ...}), 500; `e` is never referenced (unused-variable) and nothing is logged.
suggestion: Drop the unused binding or log the exception; catch sqlite3.Error rather than bare Exception.

title: books.db is created in the process CWD with no configuration hook
evidence: app.py:6 DATABASE = 'books.db' is a module-level constant; running the app or the tests from any directory silently creates/uses books.db there. Confirmed: running pytest in a scratch copy produced ./books.db.
suggestion: Make the path configurable (env var or Flask config) and document it in README.md.
